gap: No result ChatGPT got states which of these makers actually names the DC voltage its NAS takes. QNAP's own TS-233 spec page does ('Minimum 48W adapter (12VDC), 100-240VAC'). Synology's DS124 and DS223j pages give only the adapter's wattage (36 W / 60 W) and the 100–240 V AC input, never its output voltage. That leaves the TS-233 as the only maker-documented 12 V NAS among the ones ChatGPT showed.
standout_why: I compared against the pages ChatGPT cited: qnap.com TS-233 hardware specs and synology.com compare DS223/DS223j and DS124/DS223j. The QNAP page ChatGPT cited already carries the 12VDC / 48 W line, and ChatGPT used it. ChatGPT also hedged Synology as 'Verify adapter'. So the part that is new is only that Synology publishes no DC voltage anywhere I could open: the product spec page, the compare page and package contents ('AC Power Adapter x 1'). The 12 V claim for Synology rests on third-party listings alone. ChatGPT neither said this nor named QNAP's own optional replacement adapter part.
decides: It confirms the TS-233 as the only pick in ChatGPT's set whose maker states a 12 V DC input. Our page should mark Synology's 12 V input as third-party only rather than maker-stated, and should not present any Synology unit as a documented 12 V option. I could not verify UGREEN's DH2300 and DXP2800 against UGREEN pages this session, so the 12 V picks already on our page stand on their existing sources.
